title: Jamaica's Economy Shrinks 2.7% for a Fourth Straight Quarter | Across the Water, Ep. 24
lede: Jamaica's economy contracted an estimated 2.7% in July–September 2026, the fourth straight quarter of decline since Hurricane Melissa, the Planning Institute of Jamaica said on Nov 24. Mining, agriculture and tourism took the deepest hits, while remittances from the diaspora held up. The PIOJ now projects growth of 4.5% to 5.5% this quarter, largely against a low base, and has cut its fiscal-year forecast to 1% to 2%.
keyPoints: Real GDP fell an estimated 2.7% year on year in July–September 2026 and 3.2% over the first nine months, worse than the PIOJ's August forecast of a 0.5% to 1.5% decline (PIOJ, Nov 24, 2026, via Gleaner and Observer).
Mining and quarrying fell 23.5%, agriculture 18.9% and hotels and food service 10.3% in the quarter; construction grew 1.4% (PIOJ via Gleaner, Nov 24, 2026).
Stopover arrivals fell 17.9% to 572,943 and tourism earnings 12.2% to US$896.9 million; October airport arrivals were down only 2.7% (PIOJ via Gleaner and Observer).
Remittance inflows reached US$1.78 billion in the first half of 2026, up 4.2%, about two-thirds from the US (Bank of Jamaica data via Gleaner, Aug 19, 2026).
The PIOJ projects 4.5% to 5.5% growth in October–December 2026 and 1% to 2% for fiscal 2026/27, cut from 1% to 3% in August (Gleaner, Observer, Radio Jamaica).
